reason: The glucose carrier fits into the membrane and could provide a route for fuel to enter the cell.
expectation: The carrier will become part of the membrane, enabling glucose transport.

effect: The carrier is installed in the membrane, so glucose can now be tested as its transport substrate.
reaction: The fitted carrier makes the next step clear.
reason: Glucose fits the carrier's binding pocket and is more concentrated outside the cell.
expectation: Glucose will move into the cytosol through the carrier.

effect: Glucose has entered the cytosol and is available for metabolism.
reaction: The carrier’s change in shape makes its transport mechanism clear.
reason: The living cell interior contains the enzymes and mitochondria needed to connect glucose with aerobic ATP renewal.
expectation: Glucose will be used with available oxygen to renew ATP.

effect: Glucose first yields pyruvate and ATP in cytosolic glycolysis; the pyruvate is now available for mitochondrial metabolism.
reaction: The separation of glycolysis from oxygen-dependent metabolism is useful.
reason: The pyruvate is labeled as mitochondrial fuel, and the cell interior contains mitochondria and available oxygen.
expectation: Pyruvate will be used in aerobic metabolism to renew more ATP.

effect: Aerobic ATP renewal is established, and protein synthesis is now an additional goal.
reaction: The picture usefully distinguishes oxygen’s role from the fuel’s and shows the hydrogen-ion reservoir driving ATP synthesis.
reason: The sodium-potassium pump needs a membrane location before it can transport ions across it.
expectation: The pump will be installed in the membrane, ready to use ATP for ion transport.

alternatives.reason: The amino acids and existing ribosomes also suggest a route toward the new protein goal.

effect: The pump is installed in the membrane and positioned to use cytosolic ATP.
reaction: The contrast with the passive sodium channel makes its placement useful.
reason: Aerobic ATP renewal supplies energy for the installed pump to transport ions.
expectation: The pump will use ATP to move sodium out and potassium into the cell against their gradients.

alternatives.reason: Protein synthesis is another current goal.

effect: ATP-powered sodium-potassium transport is established, leaving protein synthesis as the remaining goal.
reaction: The comparison with passive sodium flow clarifies why the pump requires energy.
reason: Amino acids are protein building blocks, and the cell interior contains ribosomes and existing RNA messages.
expectation: Ribosomes will use the amino acids to make new proteins.

effect: Amino acids cannot be used directly at the cell interior; the feedback identifies ATP-related partners instead.
reaction: I had expected the ribosome location to be enough, so the energy requirement is a useful correction.
reason: Aerobic ATP renewal is an available partner and provides energy for making proteins.
expectation: The amino acids and ATP supply will support production of new proteins.

alternatives.reason: This is also listed as compatible and includes ATP.

effect: The ATP supply and amino acids produced new cell proteins, completing the remaining goal; the picture shows ribosomes following existing RNA messages and ATP supporting amino-acid preparation.
reaction: The distinct colours and inset make the roles of message, building blocks and energy easier to distinguish.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building aerobic ATP renewal was most worthwhile: the planned picture distinguishes fuel oxidation from oxygen’s role and connects the hydrogen-ion reservoir to ATP synthase.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the pump was straightforward and comparatively routine, although the later comparison with passive transport gave it context.

surprise.text: I expected amino acids to work directly at the cell interior; compatibility feedback instead pointed to ATP-related partners. The final picture clarified ATP’s role in preparing amino acids.

arbitrary.text: The need to combine amino acids with an ATP-related item rather than the ribosome-containing interior initially felt unclear. The final picture supplied a purpose, though the required pairing was not obvious beforehand.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the constructions connected membrane transport, energy renewal and protein production in useful ways. The illustration plans are informative, though they do not show whether students would understand them unaided.
